faq.q: What time does the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise depart?
faq.a: Our standard morning cruise departs Puerto Banús at 10:00 and returns at 12:00. We can adjust departure time by 30 minutes if you request it at booking. The 2-hour slot maximises dolphin activity windows.

faq.q: Which boats are used for the dolphin watching brunch cruise?
faq.a: We typically use either the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 passengers) or the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 passengers). Both are Tier A boats priced at €749 for 2 hours. You can specify your preference at booking; we'll confirm availability.

faq.q: What food and drinks are included in the brunch?
faq.a: The brunch includes an open bar of water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava, plus light snacks such as Spanish olives, crisps, and seasonal fruit. It's a light Mediterranean brunch, not a full meal.

faq.q: How likely are we to see dolphins on this cruise?
faq.a: Dolphin sightings are common year-round off the Marbella coast, especially in the morning when the sea is calm. We see them on roughly 80% of trips, but we cannot guarantee sightings as they are wild animals. The cruise is enjoyable regardless.

faq.q: Can children join the dolphin watching brunch cruise?
faq.a: Yes, children are welcome. The Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are safe, stable motor yachts. Life jackets are provided for all ages. The brunch menu includes soft drinks and snacks suitable for kids.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the day of my cruise?
faq.a: We monitor conditions closely. If the captain deems it unsafe due to high winds or rough seas, we'll reschedule your cruise at no extra cost or offer a full refund. You'll be notified at least 2 hours before departure.

faq.q: How do I book the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise?
faq.a: You can book directly via WhatsApp on our website. We'll confirm availability for your preferred date, take a deposit, and send you a confirmation with meeting point details. Full payment is due on the day.

faq.q: Is the brunch cruise private or shared with other groups?

data.body_html:
Start your morning with a Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2042 — a two-hour escape from Puerto Banús into the Mediterranean, where you'll sip cava, nibble olives, and scan the glittering water for pods of wild dolphins. Priced at a flat €749 for up to 9 guests on the Astondoa 40 or 11 on the Azimut 39, this all-inclusive experience covers skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. No hidden extras, no crowded tour boats — just your private party and the open sea.

Why Choose a Dolphin Watching Brunch Cruise in Marbella?

The Costa del Sol's inshore waters are a year-round feeding ground for common and bottlenose dolphins. Early morning, when the sea is calm and boat traffic is low, offers the highest chance of sightings. Our skippers know the local hotspots — often within 2–3 nautical miles of Puerto Banús — and cut the engines to let the dolphins approach naturally. The 2-hour format is long enough to feel unhurried but short enough to fit into a busy holiday schedule.

What's Included in the €749 All-Inclusive Price?

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and Spanish IVA (21%). The brunch element means an open bar of water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava, plus light snacks like Spanish olives, crisps, and seasonal fruit. You're welcome to bring your own food if you want something more substantial — just let us know in advance so we can provide a cooler and plates.

Which Boat Will You Cruise On?

Our Tier A fleet is ideal for this trip. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 passengers) offers a spacious sundeck and a shaded saloon, perfect for spotting dolphins from the bow. The Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 passengers) has a similar layout with a slightly larger cockpit. Both depart from Puerto Banús and are equipped with a bimini top for sun protection, a Bluetooth speaker system, and a small fridge for drinks.

Typical Itinerary: 10:00 – 12:00

Your skipper will meet you at the dock in Puerto Banús at 09:45. After a safety briefing, you'll motor out past the marina's superyachts and turn west or south-west, depending on wind and tide. The captain will slow down near known dolphin feeding areas — often around Cala del Faro or off the Río Verde estuary. After about 45 minutes of dolphin-watching, you'll cruise back towards the coast, enjoying your brunch as Marbella's skyline and the La Concha mountain come into view. Return to Puerto Banús at 12:00.

Best Time of Year for Dolphin Sightings

Dolphins are present year-round, but sightings are most reliable from April to October, when the sea temperature rises above 18°C and the baitfish move inshore. Winter trips can still be productive, though you'll want a light jacket for the breeze. Early mornings (10:00) consistently outperform afternoon slots because the sea state is flatter.

How to Book Your Marbella Dolphin Watching Brunch Cruise 2042

Ready to go? Contact us via WhatsApp with your preferred date and group size. We'll confirm availability for the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, take a deposit, and send you a confirmation with the meeting point at Puerto Banús. The balance is payable on the day by cash or card. For a longer morning at sea, consider upgrading to a 4-hour charter (€1,499) that includes a stop at Cala Cortés for a swim.
